title: Monsoon and Off-Season Marketing for Beach Properties
excerpt: Who travels to India's beaches in the monsoon, how to package and price off-season stays, how to describe the weather honestly, and how to keep guests warm for peak season.
description: Off-season and monsoon marketing for beach stays: target workations, long stays and weekenders, build packages, price honestly and keep your list warm.
html:
To market a beach property in the monsoon or off-season, target the guests who actually travel then: remote workers on workations, monsoon lovers, long-stay guests and domestic weekenders from nearby cities. Build packages for them, price for longer stays, describe the weather honestly, and keep your past guests engaged so they return in peak season.

Accept what the off-season is, then plan for it

From roughly June to September, much of India's west coast is wet, the sea is rough and swimming is often restricted. Many shacks in Goa and Gokarna close. Ferries and water activities in the Andamans can be affected by weather. You cannot market your way around that, and trying to hide it creates angry guests and poor reviews.

What you can do is stop treating the off-season as a smaller version of peak season. The guests are different, the reasons for travelling are different, and the offer needs to be different. A property that markets "beach holiday" in July is competing for very few people. A property that markets "a quiet, green week by the sea with fast Wi-Fi and a desk" is talking to a much more receptive group.

Who travels to the coast in the off-season

Look at your own past off-season bookings and enquiries first. They tell you more than any general advice. Most beach properties will find some mix of these segments:

SegmentWhat they wantWhat to show them
Workation guestsReliable internet, a proper desk, quiet, power backupMeasured Wi-Fi speed, photos of the workspace, backup details
Monsoon loversRain, greenery, waterfalls, sea views from a dry verandahMonsoon photos and video, covered seating, nearby monsoon walks
Long-stay guestsWeekly or monthly rates, a kitchen or meal plan, laundryClear long-stay pricing, what is included, house rules
Domestic weekendersA short break within a few hours' driveDrive times from nearby cities, weekend packages, parking
Wellness and retreat groupsSpace for yoga or workshops, simple food, privacyGroup rates, hall or deck photos, sample schedule

Pick two segments that match your property and write for them. A small Varkala guest house with good Wi-Fi might focus on workations and long stays. A Goa villa within driving distance of Pune and Mumbai might focus on weekenders and monsoon lovers.

Build off-season packages people can understand

A package is simply a clear bundle with a name, a price and a list of what is included. It is easier to market than "discounted rates".

Examples to adapt

  • Monsoon work week: seven nights, breakfast and lunch, desk in room, laundry once a week.
  • Rain retreat weekend: two nights, all meals, a guided monsoon walk, late checkout on Sunday.
  • Month by the sea: a monthly rate with a kitchenette or meal plan and housekeeping twice a week.
  • Small group stay: exclusive use of a block or the whole property for a group of friends or a team.

Give each package its own page on your website, with photographs taken during the monsoon, not peak-season images. Each page should state the price, what is included, the dates it applies to and how to book or enquire on WhatsApp.

Price for the season and the stay length

Off-season pricing works best when it rewards the behaviour you want, usually longer stays and midweek nights, rather than simply cutting the nightly rate. As an illustration only: if your peak rate is ₹6,000 a night, you might offer an off-season weekly rate equivalent to ₹3,500 a night, and a monthly rate lower still. The guest sees clear value and you fill rooms for longer with less turnover cost.

A few practical points:

  • Keep your rates consistent between your website and OTAs such as MakeMyTrip, Booking.com and Airbnb, or give direct guests a genuine extra (a free meal, a late checkout) rather than a hidden lower price.
  • Make the long-stay rate visible. Many guests will not ask.
  • Show the total in rupees, including taxes, so there is no surprise at checkout.
  • Accept UPI and say so. Long-stay guests often prefer to pay in instalments; state your policy clearly.

Be honest about the weather

Honest messaging is not only ethical, it is good marketing. Guests who know what to expect are happier and leave better reviews. Say clearly:

  • That the sea may be closed for swimming, and roughly which months.
  • Which nearby restaurants and shops stay open and which close.
  • Whether power cuts happen and what backup you have.
  • Whether roads near you flood or become slippery, and how guests get to you.
  • What there is to do on a day of heavy rain.

Then show what is good about the season: the green, the empty beach at low tide, the sound of rain on a tiled roof, the rates. Real photographs and short videos taken during the monsoon do more than any description. If guests post their own monsoon photos and tag you, ask permission to share them.

Where to promote the off-season offer

Off-season guests often decide closer to the date and from closer to home, so channels that reach nearby cities and existing guests work well:

  • Your past-guest list on WhatsApp and email: they already trust you and may return for a different kind of trip.
  • Google Business Profile posts announcing monsoon packages, with photos.
  • Instagram with regular monsoon content in the weeks before and during the season.
  • Small paid campaigns targeted at a few nearby cities, focused on the package pages. Our PPC management page explains how that is usually structured.
  • Remote work and long-stay communities where your offer is relevant and posting is allowed.

Our hospitality page shows how off-season promotion fits into a year-round plan.

Use the quiet months to prepare for peak season

The off-season is also when you build the demand you will need in November. Keep in touch with your list without sending discounts every week:

  • Share a short monthly update: what is changing at the property, a new room, a local recommendation.
  • Announce Christmas and New Year dates early to past guests, before they go on OTAs.
  • Collect reviews from off-season guests and reply to every one.
  • Refresh photos, update your website's seasonal pages and fix anything on the site that guests struggled with.

For the search side of peak-season preparation, read our guide to SEO for beach hotels and boutique stays.

Frequently asked questions

Should I close my beach property during the monsoon?

It depends on your costs, staff and whether there is any demand. Look at your past bookings and enquiries for those months and the fixed costs of staying open. Many properties stay open with a reduced team and a limited offer such as long stays only. If you do close, mark it clearly on Google Business Profile and OTAs.

How much should I discount in the off-season?

There is no standard figure. Start from your costs and the rate you need to cover them, then design offers that reward longer stays and midweek nights rather than cutting every night equally. Test one or two packages for a season and compare enquiries and bookings before changing them.

Is it misleading to use sunny photos in off-season marketing?

Using peak-season images to sell a monsoon stay sets the wrong expectation and often leads to complaints. For off-season pages, packages and posts, use photographs and video taken during the actual season. Keep sunny images for your general and peak-season pages.

Which off-season segment is easiest to start with?

For most properties, past guests and weekenders from nearby cities are the easiest, because they already know you or can reach you quickly. Workation and long-stay guests need more proof, such as Wi-Fi speeds and workspace photos, but tend to stay longer once they book.

Where to start

Pull your bookings and enquiries from last year's off-season and note who came and why. Pick two segments, design one package for each, and photograph the property in the rain for their pages. Send the first offer to your past-guest list on WhatsApp before you spend anything on ads.
